text.p: Frank Zarb, head of the National Association of Securities Dealers, strongly advocates eliminating the boards of directors of both the Nasdaq stock market and NASD's regulatory subsidiary, the Washington Post reported Friday.
Quoting unidentified senior NASD officials and board members, the newspaper said Zarb had not yet made a final decision.

The NASD instituted the board governing structure a year ago in response to an investigation by the Securities and Exchange Commission that concluded the NASD tolerated illegal trading practices by Nasdaq dealers.

"It has taken a Herculean effort to make the multiple-board process work," a top NASD executive told the Post. Zarb had said in the past that the two subsidiary boards of directors slowed the organization down.

"I am sure that we will end up with a structure that guarantees the principle underlying last year's reforms -- the strict separation of independent self-regulation from the operation of the market," Zarb told the Post in an interview. "That is not negotiable," he added.
NASD is a trade group for the U.S. financial industry and self-regulatory organization under SEC oversight. It runs the Nasdaq stock market as a separate unit.
